CLINICAL DOCUMENTATION — NARRATIVE EMERGENCY OBSERVATION NOTE V1
Patient: David Miller | MRN: PAT-60007 | DOB: 1962-03-08 | Gender: Male | Doc ID: NARRATIVE_0007
Encounter Date: 2025-03-21 | Discharge/Note Date: 2025-03-26 | Provider: Dr. Gregory House, MD
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PRESENTATION
Patient David Miller was triaged in the emergency department following acute onset of lightheadedness and palpitations
earlier this morning. Initial hemodynamic parameters were reviewed and patient was placed on telemetry.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
The patient describes experiencing recurrent lightheadedness over the preceding 48 hours without syncope. Initial
emergency workup revealed that initial platelet count was measured at 245.5 10*3/uL. Point-of-care laboratory screening
additionally noted potassium resulted at 6.03 mmol/L (HIGH). Given these findings, the patient was transitioned to the
Clinical Decision Unit for 24-hour observation.
OBSERVATION UNIT CLINICAL COURSE
Throughout the observation unit stay, continuous telemetry showed normal sinus rhythm without pause or tachyarrhythmia.
The patient was administered Ciprofloxacin at a dose of 250 mg PO every 12 hours for 7 days, which promptly alleviated
acute symptoms. Follow-up protocol monitoring of hemoglobin demonstrated 13.5 g/dL. Orthostatic blood pressures were
negative upon ambulation.
DISCHARGE REGIMEN
Patient was deemed safe for outpatient discharge. The ongoing regimen includes Metoprolol 25 mg oral twice daily as
prescribed. Prescription counseling was performed by nursing prior to release.
PLAN & PRECAUTIONS
Resume normal daily activities as tolerated. Avoid strenuous exercise until cardiology follow-up in 1 to 2 weeks. Immediate
emergency precautions detailed.
